question.worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set $A$ is the number of elements in $A.$ 

Notice that the elements of our set 

$$
1,\,4,\,7,\,…
$$

form an arithmetic sequence with a common difference $d=3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =3 \\  & =4-1 \\  & =7-4 \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

The $n$th term of our arithmetic sequence, denoted ${a}_{n},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =1+(n-1)\cdot 3 \\  & =1+3n-3 \\  & =3n-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can express $A$ in set-builder notation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={3n-2:n\in N,\,1\le n\le N}\end{aligned}
$$

where $N\in N$ is to be determined.

To find $N,$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}3N-2 & =295 \\ 3N & =297 \\ N & =\frac{297}{3} \\ N & =99\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ can be expressed as

$$
A={3n-2:n\in N,\,1\le n\le 99}.
$$

Finally, since $A$ has $99$ elements, we must have $|A|=99.$
